extracted.intended_audience: NYC DOT staff, regulated parties, community stakeholders, and members of the public participating in NYC municipal rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Stepwise process and timeline for amending, repealing, or adding rules of the City of New York under the City Administrative Procedure Act (CAPA), showing required approvals, publications, notice recipients, comment/hearing periods, and effective-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory agenda status
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the proposed rule appears on NYC DOT’s Regulatory Agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not on the Regulatory Agenda (e.g., pursuant to Local Law, not anticipated), the item proceeds as indicated; agenda status is a procedural flag for expected vs. unanticipated rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting by NYC DOT Legal with internal units
rubrics_metrics.description: NYC DOT’s Legal drafts the proposed rule in coordination with relevant internal units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal collaboration ensures operational, technical, and programmatic input is incorporated before external review/filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission to Law Department and Mayor’s Office of Operations (MOO)
rubrics_metrics.description: City agency submits the proposed rule to the Law Department and MOO for approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission to both offices is required before publication; their review/checks are prerequisites to certification and public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification from Mayor’s Office of Operations (MOO)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule must receive certification from the MOO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MOO certification is a formal approval step prior to publication of the Notice of Public Hearing and Opportunity to Comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification from Law Department
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule must receive certification from the Law Department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law Department certification (legal sufficiency) is required before the rule is published for public comment/hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of proposed rule (Notice of Public Hearing and Opportunity to Comment)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed rule is published as a Notice of Public Hearing and Opportunity to Comment in the City Record and NYC Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication triggers public comment and hearing timelines; publication venue is the City Record and NYC Rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public comment period (minimum 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a public comment period of at least 30 days after publication of the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By law, 30 days must elapse between the rule being proposed and the public hearing so the public can comment; this is a statutory minimum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public hearing timing (minimum 30 days from publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A public hearing on the proposed rule must be scheduled at least 30 days from the publication date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The hearing provides an opportunity for oral testimony; the 30-day minimum ensures sufficient public notice before the hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required notice recipients for proposed rule and hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Proposed Rule and Hearing information must be sent to specified parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients include: Speaker of the City Council; all City Council members; all community boards; media outlets; affected city agencies; and regulated communities (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of public testimony and written comments
rubrics_metrics.description: NYC DOT reviews public testimony and written comments submitted during the comment period and hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments are considered to inform whether the rule should be amended or adopted as proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible responses to comments (no change or amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: After review, the rule may either remain unchanged or be amended based on comments from the public hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency must document and act on substantive input; revision is optional but common if comments indicate needed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft Notice of Adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: If proceeding to adoption, NYC DOT drafts a Notice of Adoption for the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Adoption reflects the final rule text and summarizes changes made (if any) after the comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law Department review and final approval of Notice of Adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: The Law Department reviews the Notice of Adoption and provides final approval to NYC DOT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final legal sign-off is required before publication of the adopted rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of adopted rule in the City Record and NYC Rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The adopted rule and Notice of Adoption are published in the City Record and NYC Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is the formal means of informing the public of the adoption and triggers the effective-date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption recipients
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice of Adoption must be sent to designated recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients for the Notice of Adoption include: the Speaker of the City Council and affected city agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard effective date (30 days after publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule ordinarily becomes effective 30 days after the publication date of the Notice of Adoption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 30-day waiting period follows publication unless an exception is invoked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate effective date exception (Charter §1043(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: A rule can become effective immediately if necessary per NYC Charter Section 1043(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate effect is permitted when substantial need is demonstrated pursuant to Charter section 1043(f); agency must show necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall timeline estimate (75–90 days after publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the proposed rule is published, the overall rulemaking process generally takes approximately 75–90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeline breakdown: 30 days between proposal and hearing; an additional 15–30 days typically for (1) DOT to consider comments and make changes, (2) Law Department final approval, and (3) final publication; plus an additional 30 days post-publication before the rule becomes effective unless immediate effect is justified.
